title: Readiness Sprint Friction Matrix and Contingency Tracker
summary: Sprint-focused operational tracker that maps sources of launch friction to measurable KPIs, mitigations, and contingency playbooks. Designed for short (1–3 week) readiness bursts where product, SRE, and CS run a combined triage cadence.
body:
Purpose:
A compact working sheet for the next two readiness sprints (Sprint A: 2025-11-03 → 2025-11-16, Sprint B: 2025-11-17 → 2025-11-30). The goal is to surface the top friction vectors that most commonly block go/no-go gates and to attach a measurable KPI, owner, and a 3-tier contingency for each.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: Product features flagged for staged rollout (hosted API throttling changes, new model redirect logic, and console rollout changes).
- Audience: Product Ops lead, Eng SRE lead, Release Eng, Solutions Eng, Customer Success triage.

How to use this sheet (workflow):
1) Before sprint start, each owner fills current baseline KPI and estimated delta 
2) Daily standup: update status column (Green / Yellow / Red) and whether mitigation step 1 is in-flight
3) If Red at any daily check, escalate to on-call commander and initiate contingency 2 or 3 depending on severity

Friction matrix (rows = friction vectors; columns = baseline KPI | target | current | owner | mitigation-1 | mitigation-2 | mitigation-3 | status | linked-ticket):
- API throttling responses: baseline 99.95% 200s p95 success, target 99.99% | current 99.90% | owner: Oliver Hayes | mit1: tune autoscale and reclaim ephemeral workers (ETA 6h) | mit2: apply temporary rate-limit per org (ETA 2h) | mit3: route critical customers to reserved pool (manual switch) | status: Yellow | linked-ticket: JIRA-OPS-5073
- Model redirect mismatches: baseline 0.5% incorrect-routes per 10k calls, target <0.2% | current 1.1% | owner: Samir Gupta | mit1: roll back redirect config (ETA 30m) | mit2: enable canary variant with conservative routing (ETA 1h) | mit3: freeze rollout and revert to previous model (ETA 2h) | status: Red | linked-ticket: JIRA-PO-4866
- Console rollout auth regressions: baseline 99.9% SSO login rate, target 99.99% | current 99.4% | owner: Lina Rodriguez | mit1: patch token refresh logic (ETA 3h) | mit2: force session expiration + reauth flow (ETA 1h) | mit3: rollback console feature flags (ETA 30m) | status: Red | linked-ticket: JIRA-SEC-3301
- Observability gaps: baseline alerts < 1/min noise, target < 1/week false positive | current medium noise (alerts spiking during batch jobs) | owner: Eng Observability (Jason Park) | mit1: adjust alert thresholds for batching windows (ETA 4h) | mit2: temporary suppression during scheduled batch windows (ETA 1h) | mit3: emergency runbook to triage manual signals (ETA 3h) | status: Yellow | linked-ticket: GH-1192
- Customer-facing response time (CS playbooks): baseline SLA 4h initial reply, target 1h for P1 during launch | current 6h | owner: Customer Success (Mei Tan) | mit1: activate launch triage rota and templated responses (ETA 2h) | mit2: assign dedicated CS contractor team for 72h (ETA 12h) | mit3: defer non-critical inquiries to knowledge base + automated triage (ETA immediate) | status: Yellow | linked-ticket: CS-2025-11

KPI tracker (sample metrics and thresholds):
- System KPIs: p95 latency, error rate per route (errors / 1000 calls), throughput headroom (% spare capacity), rolling restarts per hour
- Business KPIs: activation completion rate (first-week), feature acceptance (net promote score within beta cohort), customer-reported blockers (tickets/day)
- Safety KPIs: data ingress anomalies, unauthorized access attempts, privacy incident signals

For each KPI record: baseline_value | alert_threshold | on_warning_action | on_critical_action | historical_trend_link
Example: p95 latency (text-generation-main): baseline 180ms | alert_threshold 350ms | on_warning_action: enable short-circuit caching for repeated prefixes | on_critical_action: reduce batch size and route to lower-latency model variant | historical_trend_link: https://observability.redwood.ai/dash/pg-main-p95

Contingency playbooks (3 tiers):
- Tier 1 (mitigation-1): fast, low-risk steps owners should attempt without leadership signoff (code toggles, config changes, autoscaler hints). Aim for < 6h to resolution.
- Tier 2 (mitigation-2): broader changes that may impact capacity or billing (temporary rate-limits, dedicated reserve usage). Requires product-ops approval; aim for < 12h to implement.
- Tier 3 (mitigation-3): rollbacks, routing critical customers to reserved pools, or delay public rollout. Requires exec notification and cross-team coordination; aim for < 24h.

Escalation matrix (quick):
- Status Yellow 48h: Product Ops lead checks in, increase pairing with owner and SRE
- Status Red immediate: Notify on-call commander, CS lead, and VP Product; open incident bridge. If contingency-2 executed, schedule patch window and customer notification. If contingency-3 executed, pause rollout and enable backout communications.

Communication templates (short snippets for rapid use):
- Customer notice (short): "We’re pausing a staged rollout to address an issue affecting X customers. No data was exposed. We expect a fix within 24 hours and will update this thread every 4 hours."
- Internal incident update: "Issue: model redirect mismatches causing incorrect model selection for ~1.2% calls. Mitigation in-flight: rolling back redirect config. Impact: degraded quality for subset of beta customers. Next update +30m."

Open questions and decisions required:
- Q1: Accept temporary rate-limits for free-tier accounts during launch? Decision owner: VP Product. Linked doc: JIRA-PO-4900.
- Q2: Is CS allowed to engage contractors for launch triage without legal review for 72h? Owner: Head of CS and Legal.
- Q3: Tolerance for fallback-to-older-model (quality delta threshold) — define numeric threshold for auto-fallback (propose 5% quality delta measured by the Eval harness).

Post-sprint actions (definition of done for a friction row):
1) KPI is back within target for 48h rolling window OR fallback in place and customer communications dispatched
2) Root cause captured in linked-ticket with remediation epic and owner assigned
3) Lessons learned note created (one-paragraph) and attached to Confluence page

Appendix: quick commands and links
- Start incident bridge: /incident create --priority P1 --component rollout
- Temporary reserve enable: infra toggle reserve-pool --org <org-id> --pool fast-reserve
- Observability dashboard (p95 & errors): https://observability.redwood.ai/d/launch-sprint/p95-errors

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact; suggestions welcome for additional friction vectors we frequently see (billing edge cases, quota artifacts, feature-flag propagation delays).
- If you add a new friction row, include a first-estimate ETA for mitigation-1 and specify which sprint it should be targeted in.

Author notes (Asha): I modeled the matrix after three recent beta rollouts — common recurring blockers were model-routing, autoscaler thrash, and console auth regressions. The emphasis here is short-cycle mitigations + clear thresholds so the on-call commander can make binary decisions quickly.
